symbols.name: \(\epsilon\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound on both conditional treatment probabilities.

symbols.name: \(M\)
symbols.def: Known envelope for cell means and unstandardized conditional fourth central moments.

symbols.name: \(\alpha\)
symbols.def: Fixed error probability for two-sided confidence intervals.

symbols.name: \(c_{\epsilon}\)
symbols.def: A positive constant depending only on \(\epsilon\).

symbols.name: \(c_0\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower constant for positive cell masses on the local triangular submodel.

symbols.name: \(v_0\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower constant for the efficient variance on the local triangular submodel.

symbols.name: \(v_1\)
symbols.def: Fixed upper constant for the efficient variance on the local triangular submodel.

symbols.name: \(K_0\)
symbols.def: A fixed number of deterministic cross-fitting folds.

symbols.name: \(c_L\)
symbols.def: A numerical coefficient in the logarithmic Chebyshev degree, selected jointly with the approximation and tail certificates.

symbols.name: \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\)
symbols.def: Absolute tolerance requested for each outward-rounded confidence-interval endpoint.

symbols.name: \(b\)
symbols.def: Number of fractional bits in each dyadic outcome enclosure.

symbols.name: \(B\)
symbols.def: Generic upper mass scale for a dyadic light-cell approximation slice.

symbols.name: \(s\)
symbols.def: Generic index of a pilot, estimation, or calibration fold.

symbols.name: \(X\)
symbols.def: Pretreatment covariate used for saturated adjustment.

symbols.name: \(P_O\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the space of \(O\)

symbols.name: \(Q_P^{(n)}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the \(n\)-fold observed-data space

symbols.name: \(\psi_1(P)\)
symbols.def: \(\psi_1(P)=\sum_{k=1}^d p_k\mu_{1k}\), the one-arm functional lower-bounded in ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal Y_{i,b}\)
symbols.space: closed intervals with dyadic rational endpoints
symbols.def: A closed dyadic interval containing \(Y_i\) whose diameter is at most \(2^{-b}M\).

symbols.name: \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}\)
symbols.space: finite binary strings encoding categorical values and dyadic rational intervals

symbols.name: \(\mathsf L_{\mathrm{in}}\)
symbols.def: Total number of bits in \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}\) and the dyadic enclosures of the known scalar inputs.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal I\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I=(I_0,\ldots,I_{K_0-1})\) has fold sizes differing by at most one; \(I_0\) is the pilot fold and the other folds support cross-fitting and direct calibration.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal K_{\epsilon,M}(B)\)
symbols.space: subsets of \(\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\)

symbols.name: \(L_n\)
symbols.def: \(L_n=\lceil c_L\log(en)\rceil\), where the numerical coefficient is selected by the approximation certificate in \(def:four-coordinate-lift-handle\).

symbols.name: \(\ell\)
symbols.def: Generic degree index in the falling-factorial recurrence.

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\mathcal L}\)
symbols.def: The categories whose pilot occupancies fall below the numerical \(\log(en)\)-order threshold in \(def:four-coordinate-lift-handle\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\)
symbols.def: Generic pair of same-class priors used in the confidence-length testing inequality.

symbols.name: \(\mathbb Q_0,\mathbb Q_1\)
symbols.space: probability laws on the \(n\)-fold observed-data space

symbols.name: \(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1\)
symbols.def: Measurable sets that contain the ATE values under \(\Pi_0\) and \(\Pi_1\), respectively.

symbols.name: \(d_n\)
symbols.def: Number of categories in row \(n\) of a triangular array.

symbols.name: \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\)
symbols.def: The law in row \(n\) is \(P_n\) and has confounder alphabet size \(d_n\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\eta^{(-s)}\)
symbols.space: pairs of cellwise propensity and outcome-regression arrays

symbols.name: \(\widehat\psi_i\)
symbols.def: The saturated-cell orthogonal score for unit \(i\) constructed in \(def:saturated-one-step\).

symbols.name: \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\)
symbols.def: The \(1-\alpha/2\) quantile of the standard normal distribution.

standard.name: independent and identically distributed superpopulation sampling

assumptions.condition: \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M\) for every \(a\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

standard.name: uniform envelope for discrete-cell outcome regressions

assumptions.condition: \(E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid X=k,A=a]\le M^4\) for every \(a\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\).

novel.justification: This is the proposal's explicitly imposed calibration regime. It permits unbounded heavy-tailed conditional outcome laws whenever their raw central fourth moments are uniformly finite, including Student-type and contaminated distributions with four finite moments. The conditional moment inequality gives \(E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid X=k,A=a]\le\{E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid X=k,A=a]\}^{1/2}\le M^2\), but the condition imposes neither a standardized-kurtosis bound nor a positive conditional-variance lower bound.

standard.name: control-arm-zero restriction used by the one-arm lower-bound experiment
scaled binary treated-outcome restriction for the one-arm hard family

assumptions.condition: \(P_n(X=k)\ge c_0/d_n\) for every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d_n\}\) and every row \(n\).

novel.justification: This explicitly imposed local regularity condition defines an intentionally restricted triangular-array submodel for first-order linearization; it is satisfied by uniform categorical designs and by stratified populations whose cell probabilities are uniformly comparable to \(1/d_n\), and it is not part of the unrestricted arbitrary-mass global class.

standard.name: growing discrete alphabet below the saturated root-sample-size boundary

definitions.name: global discrete-confounder law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}=\{P: P\text{ is a full-data probability law on }\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R^3\text{ satisfying }ass:consistency,ass:conditional-exchangeability,ass:fixed-overlap,ass:cell-mean-envelope,ass:conditional-fourth-moment\}\).

definitions.name: minimax honest expected length
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}=\inf_{C_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|C_n|]\), where the infimum is over measurable random closed intervals \(C_n=C_n(\mathcal D_n)\subseteq[-2M,2M]\) satisfying \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}Q_P^{(n)}\{\tau(P)\in C_n\}\ge1-\alpha\).

definitions.name: finite-precision rational input model
definitions.construction: \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}=((X_i,A_i,\mathcal Y_{i,b})_{i=1}^n;\text{ outward dyadic enclosures of }\epsilon,M,\alpha\text{ of diameter at most }2^{-b};\delta_{\mathrm{num}})\), where the categorical and treatment coordinates are exact, \(Y_i\in\mathcal Y_{i,b}\), \(\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal Y_{i,b})\le2^{-b}M\), and \(\mathsf L_{\mathrm{in}}\) is the total binary length of this finite string.

definitions.name: banked heavy-light lift compatibility handle
definitions.construction: Instantiate the explicit clipped linear-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator from CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026, \(thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution\), after applying it to the rescaled marks \(Y/2\) and multiplying its output by two. Rewrite its light branch through \(u_k\) as a degree-\(L_n\) element of \(\mathscr Q_{L_n}\) on dyadic slices of \(\mathcal K_{\epsilon,M}(B)\); retain its independent pilot choice \(\widehat{\mathcal L}\), fixed-multinomial falling-factorial recurrence, single independent outcome mark, zero fallbacks, and clipping, and expose the resulting light statistic as \(\widehat T_{\mathrm L}\) for direct tail calibration.

definitions.name: direct marked-factorial tail-calibration handle
definitions.construction: Use Catoni's scalar bounded-influence transform only as an algebraic score template inside independent perturbation blocks of the marked factorial lift before category aggregation. Derive the required score inequalities directly from \(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\), including cells of zero or arbitrarily small conditional variance; use observable leave-block perturbations and exponential score inversion to define \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) as the smallest radius whose two-sided score is at most \(\alpha/4\), with no cellwise union bound and no post hoc median wrapper.

definitions.name: robust heavy-light interval handle
definitions.construction: Use \(I_0\) to split categories at occupancy of numerical order \(\log(en)\); use the four-coordinate factorial lift and \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) on light cells; use saturated treated-control ratios with within-cell fourth-moment truncation and an observable self-normalized score on heavy cells; aggregate the two branches into \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}\), \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}\), and \(\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}\); return \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}=[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}},\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}+\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}]\cap[-2M,2M]\).

definitions.name: certified rational implementation of the heavy-light interval
definitions.construction: Given \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}\) satisfying \(2^{-b}M\le\delta_{\mathrm{num}}/[64n(en)^{8L_n}]\), use \(b_{\mathrm{work}}\) working bits. Generate shifted-Chebyshev coefficient enclosures by the three-term recurrence and interval Clenshaw evaluation; generate every factorial monomial by \((N)_0=1\) and \((N)_{\ell+1}=(N)_\ell(N-\ell)\), followed by multiplication by its single outcome-mark enclosure; evaluate bounded-influence and exponential scores using outward dyadic interval arithmetic; invert each monotone two-sided score by bisection on \([0,2M]\) until its bracket has width at most \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}/8\). Enlarge the exact-real endpoints from \(def:robust-heavy-light-interval-handle\) by the resulting certified arithmetic-error bounds and intersect with \([-2M,2M]\) to return \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\).

definitions.name: project-imposed balanced local triangular law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}=\{\mathbf P=(P_n)_{n\ge1}:P_n\in\mathcal P_{d_n,\epsilon,M}\text{ for every }n,\ \mathbf P\text{ satisfies }ass:balanced-cell-masses,ass:local-dimension,ass:efficient-variance-band\}\).

definitions.name: cross-fitted saturated-cell one-step construction
definitions.construction:
For validation fold \(I_s\), set \(\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}=\operatorname{clip}_{[\epsilon/2,1-\epsilon/2]}\{\sum_{j
otin I_s}A_j\mathbf1(X_j=k)/(\sum_{j
otin I_s}\mathbf1(X_j=k)\vee1)\}\) and \(\widehat\mu_{ak}^{(-s)}=\sum_{j
otin I_s}Y_j\mathbf1(X_j=k,A_j=a)/(\sum_{j
otin I_s}\mathbf1(X_j=k,A_j=a)\vee1)\); for \(i\in I_s\), let \(\widehat\psi_i=\widehat\mu_{1X_i}^{(-s)}-\widehat\mu_{0X_i}^{(-s)}+A_i(Y_i-\widehat\mu_{1X_i}^{(-s)})/\widehat\pi_{X_i}^{(-s)}-(1-A_i)(Y_i-\widehat\mu_{0X_i}^{(-s)})/(1-\widehat\pi_{X_i}^{(-s)})\); define \(\widehat	au^{\mathrm{OS}}=n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat\psi_i\) and \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}=n^{-1}\sum_i(\widehat\psi_i-\widehat	au^{\mathrm{OS}})^2\).

statements.statement: Apply CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026, \(thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution\), to the marks \(Y/2\) and multiply its clipped output by two. For \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), the resulting banked real-mark heavy-light estimator admits the four-coordinate representation in \(def:four-coordinate-lift-handle\), is computable using \(O(dL_n^3)\) arithmetic operations, and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\widehat T_{\mathrm L}-\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})]|\lesssim_{\epsilon}Md/[n\log(en)]\); its pilot misclassification contribution has the same order. The representation preserves the banked factorial coefficients, zero fallbacks, clipping, and expectation identities and exposes the selected marked-factorial statistic required by \(def:direct-calibration-handle\).
statements.justification: This compatibility lemma imports the established real-mark heavy-light approximation and verifies exactly the representation needed by the new observable tail score; it is not an independent approximation novelty claim.
statements.gap: CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026, \(thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution\), already supplies the clipped real-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator and its risk order. The remaining bridge is to expose its pilot-selected light statistic in a form on which the data-only tail calibration can act without changing the banked expectation and bias guarantees.
statements.consumer: The bias half of the globally honest upper interval and the rare-cell contribution in the \(n=9915,d=8196\) 401(k) analysis.

statements.statement: Using \(def:direct-calibration-handle\), determine the robust perturbation blocks, bounded-influence score, polynomial constants, and score-inversion critical value for which \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) is measurable from \(\mathcal D_n\) and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}Q_P^{(n)}\{|\widehat T_{\mathrm L}-E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\widehat T_{\mathrm L}|>\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\}\le\alpha/4\) together with \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\widehat R_{\mathrm L}]\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}M\{n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\). For every valid \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}\), the coefficient recurrence, factorial recurrence, outward score evaluation, and bisection in \(def:certified-finite-precision-algorithm\) must return a certified approximation to \(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) with absolute error at most \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}/4\). The tail certificate must concern the selected marked-factorial statistic itself rather than a Markov conversion of its mean squared error, a cellwise union bound, or a generic median-of-means wrapper.
statements.justification: The observable tail radius and its certified score inversion are the nonroutine bridge from sharp point risk to implementable finite-sample honest inference under the proposal's unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope.
statements.gap: Catoni2012, Sections 4.1--4.2, supplies scalar bounded-influence mean and variance score templates under its own assumptions, but does not assume or establish this proposal's uniform conditional raw fourth-central-moment envelope and does not subsume cells with arbitrarily small variance through a standardized-kurtosis argument. ShaoZhou2016, Theorem 3.1, studentizes fixed-order nondegenerate U-statistics; neither result covers a pilot-selected degree-\(\log n\) marked factorial statistic with random degeneracy.
statements.consumer: A deployable coverage certificate for sparse saturated adjustment when routine bootstrap intervals cannot reproduce unseen categories.

statements.statement: There is an interval specified by \(def:robust-heavy-light-interval-handle\) such that, for every \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}Q_P^{(n)}\{\tau(P)\in\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}|]\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\). The guarantee uses only the observed sample, the known values \(M\), \(\epsilon\), and \(\alpha\), and the conditions defining \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).
statements.justification: This is the constructive half of the honest-length frontier for arbitrary cell masses under fixed overlap and the explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Section 6 and Appendix E, reports bootstrap and Gaussian intervals but warns that they need not attain nominal coverage when \(n\) and \(d\) are comparable. ArmstrongKolesar2021, Abstract and Sections 2--4, gives finite-sample bias-aware ATE intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions and normal errors with known variance, whereas this theorem permits arbitrary categorical cell masses and only the proposal's unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope. Painsky2022 treats individual unseen multinomial masses rather than an overlap-adjusted causal aggregate with marked outcomes.
statements.consumer: A uniformly valid replacement for the reference intervals in the saturated 401(k) application of ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024.

statements.statement: For every valid input \(\widetilde{\mathcal D}_{n,b}\) with \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\le r_{n,d,M}\), \(def:certified-finite-precision-algorithm\) returns \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\) satisfying \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\subseteq\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\) and moving each endpoint outward by at most \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\). Its bit-operation count is \(O\bigl([dL_n^3+(n+d)L_n^2\lceil\log_2(8M/\delta_{\mathrm{num}})\rceil]b_{\mathrm{work}}^2\bigr)\), hence polynomial in \(\mathsf L_{\mathrm{in}}\) and \(\log(1/\delta_{\mathrm{num}})\). Consequently, its coverage is at least \(1-\alpha\) and its worst expected length is at most \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}|]+2\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\).
statements.justification: This turns the statistical construction into a finite-input algorithm with certified endpoint error and a bit-complexity bound.
statements.gap: ArmstrongKolesar2021 derives finite-sample optimal intervals by finite-dimensional convex optimization in a smoothness or shape-restricted normal regression model; it does not supply certified evaluation of a growing-degree marked-factorial statistic under arbitrary categorical masses and the proposal's unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope.
statements.consumer: A reproducible implementation for the \(n=9915,d=8196\) 401(k) table with auditable numerical error in its reported endpoints.

statements.statement: On \(\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\), \(\tau(P)=\psi_1(P)\) because \(\mu_{0k}=0\) on every positive-mass cell. More explicitly, take the control-arm-zero binary hard family used in ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, leave its zero control outcome fixed, and multiply its binary treated outcome by \(M\). The induced full-data laws belong to \(\mathcal P^{0,\mathrm{bin}}_{d,\epsilon,M}\subseteq\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\), preserve cell masses and propensities, satisfy the fourth-central-moment envelope, and multiply both \(\psi_1\)-separation and ATE separation by \(M\). Consequently the theorem's one-arm mean-squared-error lower scale \(M^2\{n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2(en)]\}\) transfers by subclass restriction to ATE point estimation for \(d\lesssim_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\). Its priors may be used in \(thm:same-class-testing-converse\) only after that theorem separately proves ATE target-set separation and prior-predictive total-variation control.
statements.justification: The source result concerns the treated-arm functional, so an explicit control-zero embedding is required before its rate can inform any ATE lower-bound argument.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, lower-bound \(\psi_1\) and use a control-arm-zero proof family; the proposition records the exact subclass and scaling identity that transfer this source experiment to the ATE model without relabeling the published estimand.
statements.consumer: The rare-cell source priors for the direct same-class confidence-length converse.

statements.statement: Let \(C_n\) be any interval satisfying the coverage constraint in \(def:minimax-honest-length\). For every pair \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) and target sets \(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1\) satisfying \(def:prior-predictive-pair\), \(E_{\mathbb Q_0}[|C_n|]\ge\Delta(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1)\{1-2\alpha-\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}_+\).
statements.justification: Uniform coverage forces a long interval whenever the observed experiments are close but their ATE sets are separated.
statements.gap: Low1997 and CaiLow2004, Theorem 1, establish coverage-to-length inequalities in nonparametric Gaussian models; this lemma states the experiment-level version needed for prior mixtures in the discrete causal model.
statements.consumer: The direct confidence-length converse, without reducing interval performance to squared-error risk.

statements.statement: For every \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), there exist priors \(\Pi_0,\Pi_1\) supported on the same class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\) and sets \(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1\) such that \(\Delta(\mathcal T_0,\mathcal T_1)\gtrsim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\) and \(\|\mathbb Q_0-\mathbb Q_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le(1-2\alpha)/2\). The rare-cell component starts from the control-arm-zero embedding in \(prop:zeng-one-arm-to-ate-reduction\), then constructs ATE-separated prior supports and verifies prior-predictive total-variation control directly; separate root-\(n\) and saturation priors complete the range. The resulting confidence-length bound \(\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\gtrsim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\) follows through \(lem:coverage-testing-inequality\), not by taking the square root of the published mean-squared-error bound.
statements.justification: This certifies the full confidence-width lower frontier in the identical raw conditional fourth-central-moment class used by the interval.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, lower-bound squared-error risk for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\). Even after the explicit control-arm-zero reduction transfers that source experiment to ATE point estimation, the published result does not place separated ATE sets inside two same-class priors or invoke uniform coverage to lower-bound expected interval length.
statements.consumer: The minimax optimality certificate for the robust interval and a diagnostic showing why shorter 401(k) intervals cannot be uniformly honest without added structure.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), \(\mathsf W^*_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\alpha}\asymp_{\epsilon,\alpha}M\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\). The exact-real interval \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\) attains the upper inequality, and for every \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\le r_{n,d,M}\) so does its certified outward-rounded implementation \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\), up to the same constant order.
statements.justification: Expected confidence length, rather than point-risk square root, is the decision-theoretic object governing honest uncertainty quantification.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2, determines a point-risk scale for \(\psi_1\), which transfers to ATE point estimation only through \(prop:zeng-one-arm-to-ate-reduction\), but it does not determine honest expected length. ArmstrongKolesar2021 gives finite-sample optimal ATE intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions with normal known-variance errors, not a frontier for unrestricted discrete cell masses under fixed overlap and the proposal's unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope.
statements.consumer: A sample-size and alphabet-size benchmark for whether saturated adjustment can support substantively informative ATE intervals.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\in\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\), \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\tau(P_n)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)+o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2})\), \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2})\), \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\to1\), and \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\to1\) in \(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\)-probability. In addition, \(\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}-z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}/n}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2})\) and \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\tau(P_n)\}/\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).
statements.justification: The same globally honest construction must recover the semiparametric first-order law when empty-cell bias is locally negligible.
statements.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Appendix A.1, records a saturated plug-in Gaussian regime while its categorical model permits arbitrary and zero cell masses; the balanced lower-mass condition here is a separately imposed local restriction used only for linearization. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML, Theorem 5.1, assumes nuisance product rates, and neither paper controls the nonlinear rare-cell correction and robust critical radius of a globally honest procedure.
statements.consumer: Efficient standard errors and familiar Gaussian reporting when the categorical table is sufficiently populated, without changing procedures across regimes.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\in\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\), \(\max\{|\inf\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}-\inf\widehat C^{\mathrm G}|,|\sup\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}-\sup\widehat C^{\mathrm G}|\}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2})\). The same conclusion holds with \(\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}_{\delta_{\mathrm{num}}}\) when \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}=o(n^{-1/2})\). Both robust intervals retain the finite-sample coverage conclusion of \(thm:global-honest-upper\) on the full class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\), including the rare-cell transition where no Gaussian approximation is imposed.
statements.justification: Endpoint equivalence makes global honesty costless to first order on the regular local submodel.
statements.gap: ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML, Theorem 5.1, proves uniform asymptotic validity for cross-fitted orthogonal-score intervals under nuisance-rate conditions, but does not connect such a local Gaussian benchmark to a finite-sample honest interval on the unrestricted arbitrary-mass class. The balanced lower-mass condition is imposed only on this proposal's local equivalence submodel.
statements.consumer: A single reporting rule for applications whose effective dimension may be uncertain: it behaves like the standard efficient interval when justified and remains honest otherwise.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\in\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\) with \(d_n=d\) fixed, the balanced-mass and nondegenerate-variance conditions remain in force, and \(thm:local-linearization\) and \(thm:endpoint-equivalence\) reduce to the classical efficient-influence-function central limit theorem, ratio-consistent variance estimation, and Wald interval for the ATE with fixed discrete covariates.
statements.justification: The fixed-alphabet reduction is the required sanity check against regular semiparametric ATE inference.
statements.gap: Hahn1998 and ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML give the known fixed-complexity efficiency benchmark; the proposition verifies that the new interval does not alter that limit.
statements.consumer: Readers can interpret the robust procedure as a strict regime extension of familiar ATE inference rather than a different estimand.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\) satisfy \(P_n\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\), \(d_n=d\) fixed, \(P_n(X=k)\ge c_0/d\) for every \(k\), and \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)/M^2\to0\). Then the valid unstudentized conclusions are \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\tau(P_n)\}\to0\) and \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)\}\to0\) in \(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\)-probability, with \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}/M^2\to0\) and \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/M^2\to0\). No standardized normal limit, ratio-consistent variance claim, or Wald endpoint-equivalence claim follows from these conditions alone.
statements.justification: This separates the valid collapsing-variance statement from the nondegenerate Wald sanity check.
statements.gap: Hahn1998 and ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML formulate regular efficiency and Wald inference under nondegeneracy; this proposition records only the unstudentized conclusion supported when the efficient variance vanishes.
statements.consumer: Applied users are warned not to report a studentized Gaussian interval merely because the discrete alphabet is fixed.

sampling_model.design: Superpopulation observational sampling with no parametric model for the categorical distribution, propensities, or outcome regressions.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment \(A\) with identification by consistency and conditional exchangeability given \(X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Fixed \(\epsilon\le P(A=1\mid X=k)\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass category.
sampling_model.outcome: Real outcomes with \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M\) and explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth central moments at most \(M^4\); this implies conditional variances at most \(M^2\) but imposes no standardized-kurtosis or positive-variance condition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Pilot-selected saturated cells, a light-cell one-mark Chebyshev factorial lift, robust heavy-cell ratios, and cross-fitted saturated empirical nuisances for the local comparator.
sampling_model.computation: Exact categorical and treatment coordinates, dyadic enclosures of real outcomes and known scalars, recurrence evaluation of polynomial coefficients and factorial terms, outward interval arithmetic, and monotone bisection to requested endpoint accuracy \(\delta_{\mathrm{num}}\).
sampling_model.randomness: All probabilities and expectations are under the observed iid sample law \(Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 lower-bounds worst-case mean squared error for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\) by the order of \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\) under fixed overlap; Appendix C.5 sets the control-arm regression to zero in the hard family.
The paper constructs heavy-light best-polynomial factorial-moment estimators attaining minimax mean squared error for additive discrete-distribution functionals.

Sections 4.1--4.2 develop scalar bounded-influence mean and variance score bounds under Catoni's stated moment and kurtosis conditions; they do not establish a uniform conditional raw fourth-central-moment envelope for a selected marked-factorial statistic.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds expected confidence length in Gaussian nonparametric experiments by a between-class modulus and the paper constructs constant-factor adaptive intervals.
Theorem 5.1 gives uniformly valid asymptotically efficient Gaussian ATE intervals from cross-fitted orthogonal scores under nuisance-rate conditions.

The Abstract and Sections 2--4 derive finite-sample optimal bias-aware ATE estimators and confidence intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions when regression errors are normal with known variance, with feasible asymptotic extensions for unknown errors.
Theorem 3.1 gives a self-normalized moderate-deviation expansion for fixed-order nondegenerate Studentized U-statistics under moment conditions.
The paper gives nearly tight dimension-free confidence intervals for probabilities of individually unobserved multinomial events.

tldr: Unrestricted categorical adjustment creates two inferential regimes inside the same identified ATE model: a regular influence-function regime when every relevant cell is populated and a rare-cell regime in which unseen categories produce an additional \(d/[n\log(en)]\) uncertainty term. The project characterizes the minimax worst expected length of uniformly honest intervals over the global arbitrary-cell-mass class with an explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope as \(M\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\), imports the accepted real-mark heavy-light Chebyshev factorial estimator as approximation infrastructure, equips its selected rare-cell statistic with a new directly observable tail certificate derived from that raw envelope, gives a certified dyadic implementation with explicit endpoint tolerance and bit complexity, proves the matching lower bound directly from same-class confidence-length tests after an explicit control-arm-zero transfer of Zeng et al.'s one-arm source experiment, and shows on a separately imposed balanced local submodel with \(d=o(\sqrt n)\) that the robust interval's endpoints merge at \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) with the cross-fitted saturated-cell Gaussian interval.

project_justification.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, establishes the large-alphabet point-risk obstruction for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\), not directly for the ATE, and Section 6 warns that the 401(k) bootstrap and Gaussian intervals may miss nominal coverage. CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026 already supplies the real-mark heavy-light approximation and point-risk infrastructure, but not a directly observable tail radius. ArmstrongKolesar2021 provides finite-sample bias-aware ATE inference after imposing smoothness or shape restrictions and normal known-variance errors; it does not cover arbitrary categorical masses under fixed overlap and the proposal's unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope. Catoni2012 supplies a scalar score template under its own assumptions, not a theorem for this raw conditional envelope or the selected marked-factorial statistic. Expected honest length is not determined by any of these point-risk results, and regular DML theory does not cover empty saturated cells.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is one interval for the unrestricted discrete model whose finite-sample calibration is proved directly from the absolute conditional fourth-moment envelope and acts on the banked selected marked-factorial statistic without standardized-kurtosis or positive-variance conditions, whose rational implementation has certified endpoint error, whose lower bound is proved as a coverage-to-testing statement in the identical global causal class after an explicit one-arm-to-ATE reduction, and whose local radius becomes the efficient Gaussian radius on a clearly separated regular submodel.
project_justification.fill: The accepted one-mark real-outcome Chebyshev factorial estimator supplies rare-cell approximation infrastructure; a compatibility lemma exposes its selected statistic without changing its bias guarantee; a bounded-influence exponential score, using Catoni only as a scalar algebraic template, supplies a data-only tail radius proved from the unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope; recurrence-based coefficient and factorial evaluation with outward interval arithmetic supplies a finite-precision certificate; a control-arm-zero scaling identity transfers the published \(\psi_1\) hard family to the ATE model before same-class ATE-separated testing priors supply the expected-length converse; and a Hajek-projection expansion on the separately imposed balanced local submodel connects the globally honest interval to the saturated one-step benchmark.

related_work: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 is the exact global-model anchor: its categorical class permits arbitrary and zero cell masses, its Theorem 2 on pages 8--10 lower-bounds the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\), and Appendix C.5 implements the hard family with the control-arm regression set to zero. Proposition \(prop:zeng\text{-}one\text{-}arm\text{-}to\text{-}ate\text{-}reduction\) records the scaling and subclass identity required before that rate can inform ATE lower bounds; the present same-class theorem must still construct ATE-separated prior supports and prove their total-variation bound. The paper's Appendix A.1 describes a saturated plug-in Gaussian regime, and Section 6 documents \(n=9915\), \(d=8196\) with uncertain interval coverage. The lower bound \(P_n(X=k)\ge c_0/d_n\) is not attributed to that paper; it is an explicit project-imposed restriction defining only the regular local submodel for linearization, variance consistency, and endpoint equivalence. CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026, \(thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution\), is reusable infrastructure: it already constructs the clipped real-mark heavy-light Chebyshev factorial estimator and proves its risk order without an additional logarithmic factor. The compatibility lemma here only rewrites and rescales that estimator so the new directly observable tail score can act on its selected marked-factorial statistic. ArmstrongKolesar2021, Abstract and Sections 2--4, is the closest finite-sample honest-ATE comparator: it optimizes bias-aware intervals conditional on realized treatment and covariates under smoothness or shape restrictions, with exact finite-sample optimality for normal known-variance errors and feasible asymptotic extensions otherwise; the global class here instead has arbitrary categorical cell masses, fixed overlap, and an explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope, so its rare-cell frontier is not a smoothness-model corollary. JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015, Section 4, and WuYang2019 provide the polynomial and factorial-moment lineage of the banked estimator, not an additional novelty claim of this proposal. Catoni2012, Sections 4.1--4.2, supplies only a scalar bounded-influence exponential-score template under its own assumptions. It neither assumes nor proves this proposal's uniform conditional raw fourth-central-moment envelope, and it does not subsume the new selected-factorial calibration when conditional variances may vanish; the score inequalities here must be derived directly from the absolute \(M^4\) envelope. Low1997 and CaiLow2004 separate honest expected length from point loss through coverage-to-testing and modulus arguments; the present converse adapts that logic to fixed-sample causal prior mixtures rather than claiming their Gaussian theorem applies verbatim. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML, Theorem 5.1, and Hahn1998 give the efficient ATE influence-function benchmark; the local result establishes endpoint equivalence to that benchmark on the deliberately balanced submodel while the global theorem covers arbitrary-mass laws outside its nuisance-rate regime. ShaoZhou2016, Theorem 3.1, informs projection and studentization but assumes a fixed-order nondegenerate U-statistic. Painsky2022 gives large-alphabet intervals for individual unseen probabilities, whereas the target here is an overlap-coupled causal aggregate with real outcome marks.
technical_internal_limitation: The explicitly imposed conditional raw fourth-central-moment envelope implies the conditional variance bound \(E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid X=k,A=a]\le M^2\) by the conditional moment inequality, but it does not imply a uniform bound on conditional kurtosis when a cell variance approaches zero. Catoni2012 therefore cannot be invoked as a black-box theorem for this model: the observable calibration must derive its score bound from the absolute \(M^4\) envelope inside the marked-factorial construction without adding positive variance. The local Gaussian claim is restricted to nondegenerate efficient variance, but the global honesty claim is not.
honest_scope: The global theorem program fixes \(\epsilon\), \(M\), and \(\alpha\), allows arbitrary and zero cell masses and real outcome laws satisfying only the stated mean envelope and the explicitly imposed unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope, and claims no adaptation to unknown \(M\) or shrinking overlap. The raw envelope implies a conditional variance upper bound but imposes neither standardized kurtosis nor positive conditional variance. Catoni2012 is used only as a scalar bounded-influence score template and is not cited as a source of this model condition or as a theorem covering the selected marked-factorial statistic. The balanced lower-mass condition is an explicitly imposed local regularity condition, not a property of the global class or an assumption attributed to ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024; it is used only for local linearization, variance consistency, endpoint equivalence, and the nondegenerate fixed-alphabet sanity check. The real-mark heavy-light Chebyshev factorial approximation is imported from CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026 and is not claimed as new. The direct rare-cell calibration under the raw envelope, robust block constants, polynomial constants, critical-value computation, and same-class confidence-length testing priors are the principal solve outputs. Zeng et al.'s Theorem 2 enters only through its stated \(\psi_1\) target and the explicit control-arm-zero subclass reduction; no ATE interval lower bound is attributed directly to that theorem. Finite-precision evaluation uses dyadic enclosures and outward rounding, so it does not restrict the statistical law to rational outcomes. When efficient variance vanishes, only the stated unstudentized collapse is claimed.
novelty_justification: CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026 already establishes the explicit real-mark heavy-light Chebyshev factorial approximation and point-risk order, so neither that construction nor its logarithmic gain is a novelty claim here. ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2, lower-bounds point-estimation risk for \(\psi_1\) over an unrestricted categorical class that permits arbitrary and zero masses; the control-arm-zero scaling proposition is the required bridge to ATE point estimation, while the paper does not characterize uniformly honest expected length or construct a directly calibrated interval. ArmstrongKolesar2021 gives finite-sample optimal bias-aware ATE intervals under smoothness or shape restrictions and normal known-variance errors, not under arbitrary discrete cell masses with fixed overlap and the proposal's unstandardized conditional fourth-central-moment envelope. Catoni2012 provides a scalar bounded-influence template but no selected-factorial tail theorem under this raw envelope, particularly when conditional variances can vanish. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML supplies the regular cross-fitted orthogonal-score benchmark but does not remain honest across empty-cell regimes. The strict increment is the directly observable tail calibration derived under the raw envelope and attached to the banked selected statistic, its certified finite-precision implementation, a matching same-class ATE confidence-length testing converse at the full root-\(n\) plus rare-cell scale, and endpointwise equivalence to the efficient saturated one-step interval on a separately imposed balanced \(d=o(\sqrt n)\) local submodel.
message: Retained the raw conditional fourth-central-moment model as an explicit calibration regime, removed Catoni as its source, and limited Catoni to a non-subsuming scalar score template. Schema, proposal-gate, LaTeX-serialization, and rendering checks pass.
